text:
Alex Chen: Thinking out loud - we should consider surfacing backpressure from continuous-batcher as 'soft hints' (priority weights) instead of hard evictions. Fewer tail flaps, simpler rollback. Thoughts?

Priya Nair: Soft hints sound good. Risk is tenant tail blowups if hints ignored. Need token accounting + predictable fallback.

Jamal Ortiz: Agree. If we keep a credit model (sliding window credits) we can throttle acceptance while preserving deadline fastpath. Credits replenish per tenant by throughput window.

Lillian Wu: Sketch of proto config we could add:

```proto
message BatcherHint {
  float priority_weight = 1;
  int32 soft_credit = 2; // tokens to prefer batching
  int32 hard_limit = 3; // optional eviction threshold
}
```

Alex Chen: Nice. Also consider hysteresis: only switch to hard eviction when soft hint consistently violated for N cycles.

Priya Nair: Telemetry needs new gauges: hint_violation_count, eviction_rate, avg_queue_age per tenant. Without that we won't know if hints are working.

Jamal Ortiz: Failure modes: if a tenant's client misreports deadlines, soft hinting could let them hog. Add short-circuit: requests with deadline < 20ms always take fastpath and bypass hint accounting.

Lillian Wu: Experiment plan: feature flag rollout (opt-in tenants), collect 2 weeks of metrics, then canary increase. CLI to enable:

```bash
redwood-cli feature set continuous_batcher.soft_hints --enable --tenants tenant-123,tenant-456
```
